name: Benjamin Y. Gerber
tagline: Top rated Workers' Compensation attorney in Atlanta, Georgia
education: The George Washington University Law School
about: As an attorney at Gerber & Elkins Attorneys at Law, Mr. Gerber provides dedicated legal representation to injured workers in Atlanta, Athens, and Columbus Georgia, and the surrounding areas. He focuses his practice on workers' compensation law.

Before receiving a Juris Doctor from The George Washington University Law School, Mr. Gerber attended the University of Georgia, where he graduated cum laude with a Bachelor of Arts in political science. During law school, Mr. Gerber interned with the United States District Court for the District of Columbia and with the U.S. Department of Justice.

Mr. Gerber understands the toll that occupational injuries and illnesses can take on workers and their families. For that reason, he strives to prepare compelling and effective claims on behalf of his clients. Mr. Gerber works closely with his clients to help guide them through the entire claims process, whether it is their initial compensation claim or they are appealing a claim denial. Having started his career defending insurance companies, Mr. Gerber understands their motivations and strategies, and he draws on this experience to help his clients obtain the compensation and benefits to which they are entitled.
In recognition of his accomplishments, Mr. Gerber has received an Avvo "Superb" rating, and he has earned a BV Distinguished* rating from Martindale-Hubbell.

Staying active in the legal community is a priority for Mr. Gerber. He serves as a junior board member with the Atlanta Volunteer Lawyers Foundation, and he is a member of the Atlanta Bar Association and the Georgia Trial Lawyers Association.

*AV Preeminent and BV Distinguished are certification marks of Reed Elsevier Properties Inc., used in accordance with the Martindale-Hubbell certification procedures, standards and policies. Martindale-Hubbell is the facilitator of a peer review rating process. Ratings reflect the confidential opinions of members of the bar and the judiciary. Martindale-Hubbell ratings fall into two categories: legal ability and general ethical standards.
